_comment: Longer essays, listed under the notes on the Writing page. Every entry must resolve to a real article. The old writings.html listed six pieces of which four had no link at all and a fifth pointed at a Medium profile rather than a post; that is why this file exists and why build.py refuses to build an entry without a url.

essays.title: What a signature does not prove
essays.standfirst: Three cases where a valid signature produced a false conclusion. Each one is a missing binding, not a missing signature.

essays.title: The approval prompt stops working after fifty clicks
essays.standfirst: Human block rates fall from about 17 percent to about 5 percent inside a single session. A control that decays the more you use it is not a control.

essays.title: The best agent detector in production catches 67 percent. Plan for the rest.
essays.standfirst: The best published number in agent security, ten months in production with zero false positives, still misses one attack in three.

essays.title: Nobody was negligent. The layer was missing.
essays.standfirst: Every party did their job correctly and the incident happened anyway, because no layer owned the question.

essays.title: The Mute Agent: why your AI needs to shut up and listen to the graph
essays.standfirst: Stop prompt-engineering safety. Move the constraint off the probabilistic model and onto a deterministic knowledge graph.

essays.title: Stop begging your AI to be safe: the case for constraint engineering
essays.standfirst: We do not ask microservices nicely to respect rate limits. Safety is an architectural constraint, not a request.
